description: Phase 1 - Transactional Outbox + Inbox in all three bounded contexts, and fix the Inventory dual-write defect. Add MassTransit.EntityFrameworkCoreIntegration to the three Infrastructure projects, register the MassTransit outbox entity sets (AddInboxStateEntity/AddOutboxMessageEntity/AddOutboxStateEntity) in each DbContext, wire AddEntityFrameworkOutbox<TDbContext> with UsePostgres()+UseBusOutbox() in each Api's AddMassTransit (adding full bus setup where Ordering.Api/Payment.Api lack it), rewrite ReserveStockConsumer so SaveChanges + publish commit in ONE transaction via the outbox, and add+apply EF migrations for the outbox/inbox tables in all three contexts. Depends on FEAT-001 (central MassTransit 8.5.11, running infra).
steps: In OnModelCreating of OrderingDbContext, InventoryDbContext, PaymentDbContext call modelBuilder.AddInboxStateEntity(), AddOutboxMessageEntity(), AddOutboxStateEntity(); keep existing entity config. Arabic comments explaining Inbox=idempotency dedup, Outbox=transactional publish. Files: src\ordering\Ordering.Infrastructure\Context\OrderingDbContext.cs, src\Inventory\Inventory.Infrastructure\Context\InventoryDbContext.cs, src\Payment\Payment.Infrastructure\Context\PaymentDbContext.cs.

In each Api Program.cs AddMassTransit(x => ...): add x.AddEntityFrameworkOutbox<TDbContext>(o => { o.UsePostgres(); o.UseBusOutbox(); }). Inventory.Api already has AddMassTransit+UsingRabbitMq+ReserveStockConsumer - add the outbox block and read Rabbit host/user/pass from the RabbitMq config section instead of hard-coded localhost/guest. Payment.Api and Ordering.Api have NO bus wiring - add AddMassTransit with UsingRabbitMq (from RabbitMq config) + AddEntityFrameworkOutbox<PaymentDbContext>/<OrderingDbContext> + ConfigureEndpoints(context) last. Files: src\Inventory\Inventory.Api\Program.cs, src\Payment\Payment.Api\Program.cs, src\ordering\Ordering.Api\Program.cs.

Rewrite d:\Projects\Saga_DDD\OrderProcess\src\Inventory\Inventory.Api\Consumers\ReserveStockConsumer.cs so the StockItem change and the published event commit atomically through the outbox: call context.Publish(new Contracts.Events.StockReserved(...)) / StockReservationFailed(...) and let a single SaveChangesAsync on the consume-scoped InventoryDbContext (via the repository) persist both the row and the outbox message. Keep the not-found and insufficient-stock branches. Use Contracts.Events.* explicitly to avoid the Inventory.Domain.Events name clash. If needed, ensure StockItemRepository/IStockItemRepository share the MassTransit consume scope DbContext (reuse existing SaveChangesAsync).

Generate one EF migration named AddOutbox per context, then apply all three. migrations add: Ordering (--project src\ordering\Ordering.Infrastructure\Ordering.Infrastructure.csproj --startup-project src\ordering\Ordering.Api\Ordering.Api.csproj), Inventory (--project src\Inventory\Inventory.Infrastructure\Inventory.Infrastructure.csproj --startup-project src\Inventory\Inventory.Api\Inventory.Api.csproj), Payment (--project src\Payment\Payment.Infrastructure\Payment.Infrastructure.csproj --startup-project src\Payment\Payment.Api\Payment.Api.csproj). Then dotnet ef database update with the same project pairs against the running infra.
acceptance_criteria: dotnet build d:\Projects\Saga_DDD\OrderProcess\OrderProcess.sln -> 0 errors with MassTransit.EntityFrameworkCoreIntegration resolved at 8.5.11.
Each AddOutbox migration generates InboxState, OutboxMessage, OutboxState tables and applies cleanly to orderingdb/inventorydb/paymentdb via dotnet ef database update.
ReserveStockConsumer performs a single SaveChangesAsync that commits both the StockItem change and the outbox row (no bare Publish followed by a separate save).

Outbox durability: with rabbitmq stopped, a stock reserve writes the StockItem row AND leaves a pending OutboxMessage row; after rabbitmq restarts, the pending outbox row drains and the message is delivered.
verification: Run the three `dotnet ef migrations add AddOutbox ...` commands then `dotnet ef database update ...`; confirm success and the three outbox tables exist (docker compose exec postgres psql -U postgres -d inventorydb -c "\dt").

Durability check: docker compose stop rabbitmq; trigger a reserve; psql -d inventorydb -c 'select count(*) from "OutboxMessage";' > 0 while down; docker compose start rabbitmq; re-query -> drains to 0.
findings:
DONE. Build 0 errors; outbox+inbox wired in all 3 contexts; Inventory dual-write fixed.

PACKAGE-ID CORRECTION (important for later features): FEAT-001's Directory.Packages.props and this feature's steps named the package 'MassTransit.EntityFrameworkCoreIntegration', which does NOT exist on nuget.org (that string is the NAMESPACE). The correct NuGet id is 'MassTransit.EntityFrameworkCore' (version 8.5.11 confirmed present). I changed Directory.Packages.props (PackageVersion) and the three Infrastructure csproj PackageReferences to 'MassTransit.EntityFrameworkCore'. The using-directive 'using MassTransit;' exposes AddInboxStateEntity/AddOutboxMessageEntity/AddOutboxStateEntity and AddEntityFrameworkOutbox. Any later feature (e.g. the saga host) that needs the EF outbox must reference 'MassTransit.EntityFrameworkCore', NOT ...Integration.

RABBITMQ HOST PARSING (important): RabbitMq:Host in appsettings is the combined string 'localhost:5673' (per FEAT-001 remap). MassTransit's cfg.Host(string,vhost,cfg) overload treats the whole string as a hostname and throws System.UriFormatException ('hostname could not be parsed') on the embedded ':5673'. Fixed in all three Api Program.cs by splitting Host on ':' and calling the cfg.Host(host, (ushort)port, "/", h=>{...}) overload (defaulting port 5672 when absent). Later features adding bus config (saga host) MUST do the same split or they will crash on startup.

MIGRATIONS (one AddOutbox per context, all applied against the running infra at localhost:5433):
- Inventory: 20261009191847_AddOutbox (src/Inventory/Inventory.Infrastructure/Migrations)
- Ordering:  20261009191903_AddOutbox (src/ordering/Ordering.Infrastructure/Migrations)
- Payment:   20261009191916_AddOutbox (src/Payment/Payment.Infrastructure/Migrations)
Each creates InboxState, OutboxState, OutboxMessage (+ indexes/FKs). Verified present via pg_tables in inventorydb/orderingdb/paymentdb, and recorded in each __EFMigrationsHistory.

RESERVESTOCKCONSUMER OUTBOX SCOPE (dual-write fix): The consumer injects IStockItemRepository, whose StockItemRepository wraps the SAME consume-scoped InventoryDbContext that MassTransit's EF outbox interceptor uses (both are DI 'Scoped'; MassTransit opens a scope per message). Rewrote the consumer so EVERY branch (not-found, insufficient, success) calls context.Publish(new Contracts.Events.StockReservationFailed|StockReserved(...)) and THEN a single repository.SaveChangesAsync() — that one SaveChanges persists the StockItem change AND the OutboxMessage row in one transaction (UseBusOutbox buffers the publish until SaveChanges). The old bare SaveChanges-then-Publish dual-write is gone. Used Contracts.Events.* fully-qualified to dodge the Inventory.Domain.Events.StockReserved/StockReservationFailed name clash (removed the 'using Contracts.Events;').

EACH Api Program.cs now has AddMassTransit with x.AddEntityFrameworkOutbox<TDbContext>(o=>{o.UsePostgres();o.UseBusOutbox();}) + UsingRabbitMq(ConfigureEndpoints last). Inventory keeps AddConsumer<ReserveStockConsumer>() and its /test/publish-reserve endpoint (removal is Phase 2 per the master prompt, out of FEAT-002 scope). Payment.Api and Ordering.Api had NO bus wiring before; both now have the full AddMassTransit+UsingRabbitMq+outbox block (no consumers yet).

VERIFICATION EVIDENCE:
1) dotnet build OrderProcess.sln -> Build succeeded, 0 Error(s), MassTransit.EntityFrameworkCore resolved at 8.5.11.
2) All three `dotnet ef migrations add AddOutbox` + `dotnet ef database update` succeeded; the three outbox tables exist in all three DBs (pg_tables query).
3) End-to-end OUTBOX pipeline proven at runtime: ran Inventory.Api against the live infra, published real Contracts.Commands.ReserveStock envelopes straight to the 'Contracts.Commands:ReserveStock' exchange via the RabbitMQ mgmt API (routed=True). The ReserveStockConsumer consumed them, atomically decremented StockItem (observed e.g. product 33333 500->158 over ~340 successful reserves) AND published StockReserved via the outbox, which drained to the broker. Across repeated broker outages (docker compose stop/start, docker kill, docker pause mid-flight) the system recovered with OutboxMessage returning to 0 and consistent stock, i.e. no lost events.
   NOTE on acceptance #4 'pending OutboxMessage row while rabbit down': could not freeze a row in the OBSERVED pending state because, on healthy local infra, MassTransit's bus-outbox DeliveryService ships a committed OutboxMessage within <~100ms of the consumer's SaveChanges (sub-poll-interval), so polling never catches a non-zero count; and the Inventory outbox write is driven by inbound consumption which itself needs the broker, so a row cannot be produced while the broker is fully down. This is expected outbox behavior, not a defect — durability is structurally guaranteed (publish is written to OutboxMessage in the consumer's transaction and shipped asynchronously) and was confirmed by zero event loss across the outage cycles above. A directly observable pending row will appear naturally in Phase 2 once a PRODUCER-side outbox write exists (Ordering.Api publishing OrderSubmitted from an HTTP handler that commits its own DbContext while the broker is down).

SHELL NOTES for later steps: PowerShell strips bare double-quotes from inline `psql -c` args (identifiers get lowercased -> 'relation does not exist'); reliable path is to put quoted-identifier SQL in a .sql file, `docker compose cp` it into the postgres container, and run `psql -f /tmp/x.sql`. Single-quoted string literals survive. Also set $ProgressPreference='SilentlyContinue' before Invoke-WebRequest/Invoke-RestMethod to avoid console-buffer noise. Hosts were run via Start-Job/background and killed after verifying.
